Illinois State Board of Elections campaign disclosure data: contributions to Monroe County's candidates since 2023

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended November 30, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($651,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to county board and county office candidates, reported to the State Board of Elections since 2023. Illinois allows business contributions. Individuals, candidates' own money, party and candidate committees, loans and other receipts are not counted.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended April 30, 2022, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Monroe County and, in most counties, the township they live in.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($17,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money is not scored: no candidates for mayor or village president, council or board, clerk and other local offices of City of Waterloo reported contributions to the State Board of Elections since 2023.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
